title: Opalite vs. Propio
summary: Per-minute billing costs more than you think. Compare Opalite Health vs. Propio on cost, speed, documentation, and clinical accuracy. August 2026.
body_markdown:
###


If your priority is instant access at the point of care, consolidated documentation, and lower per-encounter cost, Opalite Health is the stronger fit for routine and lower-acuity encounters. If your organization requires a certified human interpreter on every session, or needs in-person or ASL coverage at scale, Propio's network, expanded through its acquisition of CyraCom, is worth a close look.


###


With Propio, a provider dials into a human interpreter over the phone or by video. The session runs on a per-minute meter from the moment the interpreter picks up, which means pauses, physical exams, and chart reviews all count toward the bill. After-hours visits carry an additional surcharge on top of that base per-minute rate, so a late-evening or urgent care encounter costs more than the same visit during the day. With Opalite Health, the provider opens the app and interpretation starts immediately, with pricing that can exclude silent time and no separate after-hours rate tier. A multilingual AI scribe captures the encounter as it happens and drafts a structured clinical note for the provider to review before anything enters the record.


###


Propio is best suited for organizations that want certified human interpreters on every encounter, need in-person interpretation, or require ASL services across a large network. Opalite Health is the better fit for high-volume clinical teams that need 24/7 language access across more than 150 languages, want to reduce interpretation spend meaningfully, and need documentation and translation in one workflow instead of juggling separate vendors.


###


Propio's quality rests on interpreter training standards and professional codes of ethics, without encounter-level AI quality monitoring. Opalite Health runs every session through Opalite Guardian, an automated safety framework that checks for omissions, negation errors, numeral errors including dosages, hallucinations, and low-confidence outputs in real time. In an independent validation study with Johns Hopkins Medicine, Opalite produced more than 90% fewer major and critical errors compared with certified medical interpreters in that study.


###


Opalite Health covers routine and lower-acuity encounters immediately and at scale, across more than 150 languages, with automated quality controls running on every session. Complex informed consent and end-of-life discussions can also be handled by Opalite when appropriate quality safeguards are active. For acute psychiatric crises and encounters where the patient requests a human interpreter, your organization should define a clear escalation policy so those visits reach a qualified human interpreter. That division of labor lets your team deploy AI as the default and reserve human interpretation for the situations that genuinely call for it.
